questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: What is a skeleton?
questions.a: A skeleton is the framework of bones that supports the body and gives it shape.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Name the two main parts of the human skeleton.
questions.a: The axial skeleton and the appendicular skeleton.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Name any four bones found in the arm and hand.
questions.a: Any four of: humerus, radius, ulna, carpals, metacarpals, phalanges.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Name the longest bone and the smallest bone in the human body.
questions.a: Longest — the femur; smallest — the stapes in the middle ear.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Give the three types of joints according to movement, with one example of each.
questions.a: Immovable — joints of the cranium; slightly movable — joints between the vertebrae; freely movable — the shoulder joint.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Name the four types of freely movable joints.
questions.a: Ball and socket, hinge, pivot and gliding.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Give the difference between a ligament and a tendon.
questions.a: A ligament joins bone to bone, while a tendon joins muscle to bone.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Differentiate between voluntary and involuntary muscles.
questions.a: Voluntary muscles are under our control, for example the arm muscles; involuntary muscles work on their own, for example the muscles of the stomach.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Which muscles work together to bend and straighten the arm?
questions.a: The biceps and the triceps. The biceps contracts to bend the arm, and the triceps contracts to straighten it.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: State any four functions of the muscular–skeletal system.
questions.a: Any four of: support, giving shape, protection of organs, movement, production of blood cells, storage of minerals, attachment of muscles.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Name the disease caused by lack of vitamin D and calcium in children and give one sign.
questions.a: Rickets — the child has bent (bowed) legs and soft, weak bones.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Name the four types of fractures.
questions.a: Simple (closed), compound (open), greenstick and comminuted.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Give the first aid you would give to a person with a fractured arm.
questions.a: Keep the person calm and still, do not try to push the bone back, support the arm with a splint and a sling, control any bleeding, and take the person to a health worker immediately.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Give three ways of keeping the muscular–skeletal system healthy.
questions.a: Any three of: eat a balanced diet rich in calcium and protein, get vitamin D from morning sunshine, exercise regularly, rest enough, avoid accidents, immunise against polio, keep correct posture.
accepted: eat a balanced diet rich in calcium and protein
get vitamin D from morning sunshine

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: State any three importances of correct posture.
questions.a: Any three of: it keeps the backbone straight, it prevents back and neck pain, it allows the lungs to work properly, it prevents deformities, it makes a person look smart.
accepted: it prevents back and neck pain
it allows the lungs to work properly
it makes a person look smart

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Define electricity and name its two types.
questions.a: Electricity is a form of energy caused by the movement of electrons. Its two types are static electricity and current electricity.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Give any four sources of electricity used in Uganda.
questions.a: Any four of: dry cells, hydro-electric power, solar panels, wind, generators, geothermal, thermal (fossil fuels), biogas.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Give the difference between a conductor and an insulator, with one example of each.
questions.a: A conductor allows electricity to pass through it, for example copper; an insulator does not, for example rubber.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Draw and label a simple electric circuit. (Cell, switch, bulb and connecting wires.)
questions.a: Learner's drawing. It should show a cell, connecting wires, a switch and a bulb forming a complete (closed) loop.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Give two differences between a series circuit and a parallel circuit.
questions.a: In a series circuit the bulbs are in one path, so if one blows all go off and the bulbs are dimmer. In a parallel circuit each bulb is on its own branch, so if one blows the others stay on and the bulbs are brighter.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: What is a short circuit, and give two of its causes?
questions.a: A short circuit is when current finds a shorter path of very little resistance and flows without passing through the appliance. Causes: worn out or bare wires touching, water reaching the wires, overloading a socket, poor wiring.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: State any four safety precautions in handling electricity.
questions.a: Any four of: never touch switches with wet hands; do not put metal objects in sockets; do not overload sockets; replace worn out wires; switch off the mains before repairs; keep children away from sockets; never touch fallen power lines.
accepted: never touch switches with wet hands
do not put metal objects in sockets
switch off the mains before repairs

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Give any four uses of electricity in a home.
questions.a: Any four of: lighting, cooking, ironing, refrigeration, pumping water, running radios and televisions, charging phones, running computers.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Name any four magnetic materials.
questions.a: Iron, steel, nickel and cobalt.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Give the difference between natural and artificial magnets, with one example of each.
questions.a: Natural magnets are found in the ground, for example lodestone; artificial magnets are made by people, for example a bar magnet.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: State the law of magnetism.
questions.a: Like poles repel and unlike poles attract.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Describe how you would make a magnet by the stroking method.
questions.a: Place the steel bar on a table. Take one pole of a strong magnet and stroke the bar from one end to the other, always in the same direction, lifting the magnet high at the end of each stroke. Repeat many times; the bar becomes a magnet.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Give three ways in which a magnet can lose its magnetism.
questions.a: Any three of: heating it strongly, hammering or dropping it repeatedly, passing alternating current through it, storing it carelessly.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: How are magnets properly stored?
questions.a: Bar magnets are stored in pairs with unlike poles facing each other and soft iron keepers placed across the ends.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Explain briefly how an electric bell works.
questions.a: When the switch is pressed, current flows through the electromagnet, which attracts the soft iron armature so that the hammer hits the gong. This movement breaks the circuit, the electromagnet loses its magnetism and the spring pulls the armature back, closing the circuit again. The action repeats quickly, so the bell rings continuously.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Define energy and name any four forms of energy.
questions.a: Energy is the ability to do work. Forms: heat, light, sound, electrical, chemical, mechanical (any four).

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: What is the main source of energy on earth?
questions.a: The sun.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Name three energy resources obtained from water.
questions.a: Hydro-electric power, steam energy and tidal energy.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Name the three fossil fuels.
questions.a: Coal, petroleum (crude oil) and natural gas.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Give two disadvantages of using fossil fuels.
questions.a: They pollute the air and cause global warming; they are non-renewable and will get used up. (Also: mining and drilling damage the environment.)

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Name two energy resources obtained from plants.
questions.a: Any two of: firewood, charcoal, biofuel (ethanol or biodiesel), biogas from plant waste, crop residues such as bagasse.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: What is biogas and how is it made?
questions.a: Biogas is a gas produced when animal dung or other organic waste rots in a digester without air. The gas is piped away and burnt for cooking and lighting.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Give three advantages of using biogas.
questions.a: Any three of: it is cheap and renewable; it uses waste; the slurry left over is good manure; it reduces the cutting of trees; it burns cleanly without smoke.
accepted: the slurry left over is good manure
it reduces the cutting of trees

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Give two ways in which animals provide energy.
questions.a: Animals give muscle energy — oxen ploughing, donkeys carrying loads — and their dung is used to make biogas.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Give the difference between renewable and non-renewable energy resources.
questions.a: Renewable resources can be replaced or never run out, such as solar and wind; non-renewable resources get used up and cannot be replaced, such as coal and oil.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Classify these as renewable or non-renewable: solar, coal, wind, natural gas.
questions.a: Renewable: solar, wind. Non-renewable: coal, natural gas.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Name three hydro-electric power stations in Uganda.
questions.a: Any three of: Nalubaale, Kiira, Bujagali, Isimba, Karuma.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Give two advantages and two disadvantages of hydro-electric power.
questions.a: Advantages: it is renewable and it does not pollute the air (also cheap to run, and the dam stores water). Disadvantages: dams are very expensive to build and they may flood people's land (also affected by drought).

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: State any four importances of energy resources.
questions.a: Any four of: cooking and lighting, running industries, transport, pumping water, powering hospitals and schools, communication, creating jobs, farm work.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Suggest four ways of conserving energy in your home or school.
questions.a: Any four of: switch off lights and appliances not in use; use energy-saving bulbs and stoves; use solar or biogas instead of firewood; plant trees for firewood; cover pots while cooking; service vehicles regularly; walk or share transport for short journeys.
accepted: switch off lights and appliances not in use

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: What is a simple machine? Give two ways in which machines make work easier.
questions.a: A simple machine is a device that makes work easier. It allows a small effort to move a big load, and it can change the direction of the force applied.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Define effort, load and fulcrum.
questions.a: Effort is the force applied to the machine; load is the weight or resistance the machine works against; fulcrum is the fixed point about which a lever turns.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: A load of 800 N is lifted by an effort of 200 N. Find the mechanical advantage.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: A machine has a mechanical advantage of 6. What effort is needed to lift a load of 540 N?
questions.a: Effort = 540 ÷ 6 = 90 N

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: State the principle of moments.
questions.a: Load × distance of the load from the fulcrum = effort × distance of the effort from the fulcrum.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: A load of 50 N is 3 m from the fulcrum. Find the effort acting 5 m from the fulcrum on the other side.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Name the three classes of levers and give one example of each.
questions.a: First class — see-saw or scissors; second class — wheelbarrow; third class — fishing rod.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Name the class of lever to which a pair of pliers belongs.
questions.a: First class (the fulcrum is between the effort and the load).

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: What is an inclined plane, and give two examples?
questions.a: An inclined plane is a slanting surface used to raise a load. Examples: a ramp and a plank used to roll a drum onto a lorry (also staircases and zigzag hill roads).

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Give two examples each of a wedge and a screw.
questions.a: Wedge: axe, knife (also panga, nail, chisel). Screw: bolt and nut, screw jack (also vice, corkscrew).

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Give the difference between a fixed pulley and a movable pulley.
questions.a: A fixed pulley only changes the direction of the force, so the effort equals the load; a movable pulley reduces the effort needed, giving a mechanical advantage of about 2.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Give three examples of a wheel and axle.
questions.a: Any three of: steering wheel, door knob, bicycle wheel and pedals, windlass on a well, tap handle, screwdriver.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Define friction and give three examples of friction in daily life.
questions.a: Friction is the force that opposes movement between two surfaces in contact. Examples: brakes stopping a bicycle; shoes gripping the ground when walking; a match lighting when struck.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Give three ways of increasing friction and three ways of reducing it.
questions.a: Increase: make surfaces rougher; put treads on tyres and shoes; press the surfaces together more firmly. Reduce: lubricate with oil or grease; use ball bearings or rollers; polish surfaces or streamline the shape.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Give two disadvantages of friction.
questions.a: It wears out tyres, shoes and machine parts, and it wastes energy as heat, so machines use more fuel. (It also causes noise and overheating.)

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Define excretion and give the difference between excretion and egestion.
questions.a: Excretion is the removal of waste products made inside the body. Egestion is the removal of undigested food (faeces), which was never part of the body's chemical processes.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Name the four excretory organs and the waste each one removes.
questions.a: Skin — sweat; kidneys — urine; lungs — carbon dioxide and water vapour; liver — bile pigments (and it makes urea).

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Name the two main layers of the human skin.
questions.a: The epidermis and the dermis.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Name any four parts found in the dermis.
questions.a: Any four of: sweat glands, sebaceous glands, hair follicles, blood vessels, nerve endings, fatty layer.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: State any four functions of the skin.
questions.a: Any four of: excretion of sweat, control of body temperature, protection against germs and injury, sensation, formation of vitamin D, storage of fat and water.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Name any three skin diseases and the cause of each.
questions.a: Any three, for example: scabies — mites; ringworm — a fungus; boils — bacteria; athlete's foot — a fungus; eczema — allergy or irritation.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Give four ways of caring for the skin.
questions.a: Any four of: bathe daily with soap and clean water; wear clean clothes; cut nails short; treat wounds early; eat a balanced diet and drink water; avoid sharing towels and combs; wear shoes.
accepted: bathe daily with soap and clean water
eat a balanced diet and drink water

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Name the four parts of the urinary system in the order urine passes through them.
questions.a: Kidneys → ureters → urinary bladder → urethra.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Name any three parts of a kidney.
questions.a: Any three of: cortex, medulla, pelvis, nephrons, renal artery, renal vein.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: State any three functions of the kidney.
questions.a: Any three of: filtering the blood, removing urea and excess salts, forming urine, controlling the amount of water in the body.
accepted: controlling the amount of water in the body

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Name any three diseases or disorders of the kidney.
questions.a: Any three of: kidney stones, nephritis, kidney failure, bilharzia, cystitis.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: How is kidney failure treated?
questions.a: By dialysis — cleaning the blood using a machine — or by a kidney transplant.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Which two wastes do the lungs remove?
questions.a: Carbon dioxide and water vapour.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Name any three diseases of the lungs and give one way of preventing lung disease.
questions.a: Any three of: tuberculosis, pneumonia, bronchitis, asthma, lung cancer, whooping cough. Prevention: do not smoke, keep rooms well ventilated, avoid smoke and dust, and immunise children.
accepted: whooping cough. Prevention: do not smoke

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Give any four good habits that keep the excretory system working well.
questions.a: Any four of: drink plenty of clean water; eat a balanced diet with little salt; bathe daily; exercise regularly; avoid alcohol, smoking and drug abuse; do not hold urine too long; go for medical check-ups.
accepted: eat a balanced diet with little salt
do not hold urine too long

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Define light and give two natural and two artificial sources of light.
questions.a: Light is a form of energy that enables us to see. Natural: the sun, lightning (also stars, fireflies). Artificial: electric bulb, candle (also torch, lantern).

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Give the difference between a luminous and a non-luminous body.
questions.a: A luminous body produces its own light, for example the sun; a non-luminous body does not produce light but is seen when light falls on it, for example the moon.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: How does light travel? Describe one experiment that proves it.
questions.a: Light travels in straight lines. Take three cards with holes punched at the same height, line them up with a candle behind them; the candle is seen only when the three holes are in a straight line. When one card is moved, the light is blocked.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Give the difference between transparent, translucent and opaque materials, with one example of each.
questions.a: Transparent lets nearly all light through (clear glass); translucent lets only some light through (frosted glass or oiled paper); opaque lets no light through (wood).

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: What three things are needed for a shadow to form?
questions.a: A source of light, an opaque object and a screen.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Give the difference between a solar eclipse and a lunar eclipse.
questions.a: In a solar eclipse the moon comes between the sun and the earth. In a lunar eclipse the earth comes between the sun and the moon.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Describe the image formed by a pin-hole camera.
questions.a: It is real, inverted (upside down), laterally inverted and smaller than the object.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: State the two laws of reflection.
questions.a: (i) The angle of incidence is equal to the angle of reflection. (ii) The incident ray, the reflected ray and the normal all lie in the same plane.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Give four characteristics of an image formed by a plane mirror.
questions.a: It is virtual, upright, the same size as the object, laterally inverted, and as far behind the mirror as the object is in front (any four).

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: How does a periscope work?
questions.a: It has two plane mirrors fixed at 45° facing each other. Light from the object strikes the top mirror and is reflected down to the lower mirror, which reflects it into the eye of the observer.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: What is refraction? Give three of its effects.
questions.a: Refraction is the bending of light as it passes from one transparent material to another. Effects: a stick in water looks bent; a pool looks shallower than it is; a coin in water appears raised; dispersion and the rainbow (any three).

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Name the seven colours of white light in order.
questions.a: Red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, violet.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Name the two types of lenses and give one use of each.
questions.a: Convex (converging) — used in a magnifying glass and cameras; concave (diverging) — used in spectacles for short sight.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Name any five parts of the human eye and give the work of each.
questions.a: Any five, for example: cornea — lets light in and starts bending it; iris — controls the size of the pupil; pupil — lets light into the eye; lens — focuses light on the retina; retina — where the image is formed; optic nerve — carries the message to the brain.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Name two eye defects and how each is corrected.
questions.a: Short sight is corrected with concave lenses; long sight is corrected with convex lenses.

topics.title: Interdependence of Things in the Environment

questions.subject: SCI
questions.topic: Interdependence of Things in the Environment
questions.q: Define the environment and name its two components.
questions.a: The environment is everything that surrounds a living thing. Its components are the living (biotic) and the non-living (abiotic).

questions.subject: SCI
questions.topic: Interdependence of Things in the Environment
questions.q: Give three ways in which animals depend on plants.
questions.a: Any three of: plants give animals food; plants give out oxygen; plants provide shelter and nesting materials; plants provide medicine and shade.
accepted: plants provide shelter and nesting materials

questions.subject: SCI
questions.topic: Interdependence of Things in the Environment
questions.q: Give three ways in which plants depend on animals.
questions.a: Any three of: animals give out carbon dioxide used in photosynthesis; animal droppings and dead bodies make the soil fertile; animals pollinate flowers; animals disperse seeds; people plant and protect crops; burrowing animals aerate the soil.
accepted: animals give out carbon dioxide used in photosynthesis
animal droppings and dead bodies make the soil fertile

questions.subject: SCI
questions.topic: Interdependence of Things in the Environment
questions.q: Give two ways in which plants depend on other plants.
questions.a: Big trees give shade and shelter to smaller plants; climbing plants use others for support; fallen leaves rot into humus that feeds other plants; legumes add nitrogen to the soil (any two).

questions.subject: SCI
questions.topic: Interdependence of Things in the Environment
questions.q: Write down a food chain with four members.
questions.a: For example: grass → grasshopper → lizard → hawk.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.topic: Interdependence of Things in the Environment
questions.q: What is a producer? What is a decomposer?
questions.a: A producer is a green plant that makes its own food. A decomposer is an organism such as bacteria or fungi that rots dead matter and returns nutrients to the soil.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.topic: Interdependence of Things in the Environment
questions.q: Give the difference between a food chain and a food web.
questions.a: A food chain shows one single path of food energy, while a food web is many food chains joined together, showing that animals feed on more than one thing.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.topic: Interdependence of Things in the Environment
questions.q: Give three ways in which plants depend on non-living things.
questions.a: Plants use soil for anchorage and mineral salts, water for photosynthesis and transport, air for carbon dioxide, and sunlight as the energy for photosynthesis (any three).

questions.subject: SCI
questions.topic: Interdependence of Things in the Environment
questions.q: Give two ways in which non-living things benefit from living things.
questions.a: Dead plants and animals add humus and make the soil fertile; plant roots hold the soil and prevent erosion; plants release oxygen and water vapour into the air (any two).

questions.subject: SCI
questions.topic: Interdependence of Things in the Environment
questions.q: Define agroforestry and name its three types.
questions.a: Agroforestry is the growing of trees together with crops and/or animals on the same piece of land. Types: agri-silviculture, silvo-pastoral and agro-silvo-pastoral.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.topic: Interdependence of Things in the Environment
questions.q: State any five importances of agroforestry.
questions.a: Any five of: provides firewood, timber and poles; gives shade and windbreaks; leaves make manure; roots control soil erosion; legumes add nitrogen; provides fodder, fruits and medicine; brings extra income; attracts rainfall; uses land productively.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.topic: Interdependence of Things in the Environment
questions.q: Give three ways of caring for trees on an agroforestry farm.
questions.a: Any three of: watering seedlings, weeding and mulching, pruning branches, fencing against animals, applying manure, controlling pests and diseases, thinning.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.topic: Interdependence of Things in the Environment
questions.q: Give the difference between pollarding and coppicing.
questions.a: Pollarding is cutting off the top branches and leaving the trunk standing, while coppicing is cutting the whole tree close to the ground so that new shoots grow from the stump.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.topic: Interdependence of Things in the Environment
questions.q: Outline any five steps in managing a school wood project.
questions.a: Any five of: choose a suitable site; prepare a nursery bed and sow seeds; prepare the land and mark the spacing; transplant at the start of the rains; water and mulch; weed regularly; fence and protect from fire and animals; prune and thin; control pests; keep records; harvest properly and replant.
accepted: prepare a nursery bed and sow seeds
prepare the land and mark the spacing
transplant at the start of the rains
fence and protect from fire and animals

questions.subject: SCI
questions.topic: Interdependence of Things in the Environment
questions.q: Give three benefits of a school wood project.
questions.a: Any three of: it supplies firewood and poles for the school; it teaches learners practical skills; it earns the school money; it gives shade and beautifies the compound; it protects the soil and the environment.
accepted: it supplies firewood and poles for the school
it gives shade and beautifies the compound
it protects the soil and the environment

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Name any five common sicknesses in a home and give the cause of each.
questions.a: Any five, for example: malaria — a parasite carried by the mosquito; diarrhoea — germs in dirty food and water; typhoid — bacteria in contaminated food or water; worms — worm eggs from dirty hands or bare feet; cough and flu — viruses; scabies — mites.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: How is malaria spread and how can it be prevented at home?
questions.a: Malaria is spread by the bite of an infected female anopheles mosquito. It is prevented by sleeping under a treated mosquito net, draining stagnant water, clearing bushes around the house, closing windows early, and getting tested and treated early.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Give four ways of controlling common sicknesses in a home.
questions.a: Any four of: keep the home clean; use a latrine and wash hands with soap; boil or treat drinking water; cover food; sleep under a treated net; immunise children; eat a balanced diet; go to a health centre early.
accepted: use a latrine and wash hands with soap
go to a health centre early

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Name any four health and social problems facing young people today.
questions.a: Any four of: early pregnancy and early marriage, drug and substance abuse, HIV/AIDS and other STIs, defilement and sexual abuse, poor hygiene, child labour, peer pressure, poor nutrition.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: What is anti-social behaviour? Give four examples.
questions.a: Anti-social behaviour is behaviour that harms other people or the community. Examples: stealing, bullying, drug abuse, vandalism, fighting, truancy, gambling (any four).

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Give three effects of drug abuse on a young person.
questions.a: Any three of: poor health and addiction; poor performance and dropping out of school; involvement in crime and accidents; loss of money; broken relationships with family and friends.
accepted: poor performance and dropping out of school
broken relationships with family and friends

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Give three ways of preventing anti-social behaviour among young people.
questions.a: Any three of: guidance and counselling; using free time well in sports and clubs; choosing friends wisely and resisting peer pressure; obeying school and community rules; religious and moral teaching; reporting wrongdoing.
accepted: using free time well in sports and clubs
choosing friends wisely and resisting peer pressure

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: What should a child do if an adult tries to touch his or her private parts?
questions.a: The child should say NO firmly, get away from the person, and tell a trusted adult at once — a parent, teacher, health worker, religious leader or the police. The child should not keep it secret; it is never the child's fault.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: What is a health survey? Give four steps followed in carrying one out.
questions.a: A health survey is the collecting of information about the health problems of a community so that they can be solved. Steps: choose the problem; prepare questions or a checklist; get permission from leaders; visit homes and record observations; organise the findings in tables or graphs; report to the community and health workers; suggest and take action (any four).

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Give three activities, other than a survey, used to address health concerns in a community.
questions.a: Any three of: health education talks and radio programmes; immunisation campaigns; clean-up days; digging latrines and rubbish pits; protecting water sources; distributing mosquito nets; guidance and counselling.
accepted: health education talks and radio programmes

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Define population and census.
questions.a: Population is the total number of people living in a place at a particular time. A census is the official counting of all the people in a country.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Give three ways of collecting information about the population.
questions.a: Any three of: a national census; birth and death registers; health centre records; school registers; surveys and questionnaires; local council records.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Give four reasons why a country needs population information.
questions.a: Any four of: to plan for schools, hospitals, water and roads; to know the population growth rate; to plan for food and jobs; to share government services and funds fairly; to plan immunisation and other health services.
accepted: to know the population growth rate
to plan for food and jobs
to share government services and funds fairly
to plan immunisation and other health services

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Give four problems caused by a rapidly growing population.
questions.a: Any four of: overcrowding and slums; pressure on schools, hospitals and water; unemployment and poverty; food shortage; land shortage and conflicts; destruction of forests and wetlands; fast spread of disease.

questions.subject: SCI
questions.q: Name any five activities of a school health club.
questions.a: Any five of: cleaning the compound and latrines; checking personal hygiene; running hand-washing points; making health posters; performing drama, songs and poems; inviting health workers to give talks; growing vegetables and fruit; carrying out health surveys; keeping a first-aid box.
accepted: inviting health workers to give talks
